name: Wipro

roles.name: Elite NTH – Project Engineer
roles.note: Wipro describes Elite as its technical graduate hiring program for newly graduated engineers. Secondary sources commonly cite ~₹3.5 LPA; verify in your offer.

roles.name: Turbo – (Senior) Project Engineer
roles.note: Higher track. Secondary sources describe the same test with a higher cutoff, possibly extra advanced coding, and a harder technical interview; reported CTC figures vary (~₹5.5–6.5 LPA).

rounds.name: Aptitude Test (Quant, Logical, Verbal)
rounds.what_they_check: Core aptitude and English. Older breakdowns (Hitbullseye) give ~48 minutes for aptitude within a ~128-minute test; a 2026 guide gives 60 minutes. Per-section question counts conflict across sources.
prep: Practise speed arithmetic: percentages, averages, ratios, time & work.
Practise logical sets: coding-decoding, series, seating arrangement.
Practise grammar, synonyms/antonyms and short reading comprehension passages.

rounds.name: Written Communication Test (Essay)
rounds.what_they_check: Structured written English: grammar, coherence and staying on topic. PrepInsta and Hitbullseye both list ~20 minutes.
prep: Practise 200–300 word essays with an intro–body–conclusion structure in 20 minutes.
Proofread for grammar, spelling and sentence length before submitting.
Prepare simple opinion structures for common topics (technology, education, environment).

rounds.name: Online Programming Test
rounds.what_they_check: Ability to write two working programs in Java, C, C++ or Python (per PrepInsta/Hitbullseye). One secondary source says Turbo adds an extra advanced coding section; this is unconfirmed.
prep: Practise easy–medium problems on arrays, strings, number theory and patterns.
Handle edge cases and input format exactly as stated.
For Turbo, add medium-level DSA (sorting, hashing, recursion).

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.what_they_check: Programming fundamentals, your project, and CS basics; reported to be harder for Turbo.
prep: Revise OOP, DBMS/SQL and one language in depth.
Be ready to explain the code you wrote in the online test.
Prepare a clear walkthrough of your project.

rounds.name: HR Interview
rounds.what_they_check: Communication, flexibility on location/shifts, and understanding of the service agreement and offer terms.
prep: Prepare answers on relocation and shift work.
Read and understand the service agreement terms before the interview.

cutoffs.note: Not published; Wipro has not officially disclosed cutoffs (FACE Prep). One prep site reports sectional minimums (notably verbal) and projects ~62–67% for Elite in 2026, but labels these as estimates/projections, so no number is given here.

cse_it.note: Coding test is part of the process for everyone; CSE/IT candidates should aim for Turbo-level performance.

ece_eee.note: Elite targets engineering graduates; confirm your branch is in the current notice. The two-program coding test still applies.

mech_civil.note: Generally eligible as B.E/B.Tech graduates (confirm in notice); must still clear the coding test, so practise basic programs in one language.

all.note: Secondary sources cite 60% in 10th and 12th, 60% or 6.0 CGPA in graduation, full-time courses only, and at most one backlog at test time. Verify on careers.wipro.com.

jd_skills.note: Verbal section; a sectional minimum is reported.
One of Java, C, C++ or Python for the programming test.
Helpful talking point; not a stated requirement.
Can strengthen your profile; not required.

hr_focus: Service agreement: secondary sources report a 12-month service agreement for Elite/Turbo; read the exact terms in your offer letter.
Willingness to relocate and work in shifts.
Why Wipro, and Elite vs Turbo expectations.
